questions.stem: What does a spacecraft structure support?
options: Equipment and mechanical loads during launch
Only the mission data sent by radio
Electrical energy during an eclipse
The measurement of spacecraft attitude
questions.explanation: The structure holds the hardware and must withstand loads such as launch vibration and acceleration.

questions.stem: Why does a spacecraft use batteries?
options: To provide the primary mechanical structure
To point an antenna toward a ground station
To reject heat directly into space
To store electrical energy for periods when generation is insufficient
questions.explanation: Batteries store electrical energy and can supply loads during an eclipse or other low-generation period.

questions.stem: What does a spacecraft reaction wheel help control?
options: The spacecraft position through continuous linear thrust
The temperature of a radiator
The orientation of the spacecraft
The amount of propellant stored in a tank
questions.explanation: Changing the rotational momentum of a reaction wheel produces an opposing rotational effect on the spacecraft.

questions.stem: Why may a spacecraft need to manage reaction-wheel momentum?
options: A wheel can store unlimited angular momentum.
A wheel has a finite operating-speed range.
Wheel speed has no effect on angular momentum.
Attitude control removes all external disturbance torques.
questions.explanation: Wheels have operational limits; a spacecraft may use another actuator to remove accumulated momentum.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of an attitude sensor?
options: Help determine the orientation of the spacecraft
Provide thrust for an orbital manoeuvre
Store energy during sunlight
Transmit telemetry to the ground
questions.explanation: Attitude sensors provide measurements used to estimate orientation and support control.

questions.stem: What is the job of the communications subsystem of a spacecraft?
options: Store electrical energy during sunlight
Measure the temperature of the cabin
Change the orientation using angular momentum
Exchange information with another station
questions.explanation: Communications equipment handles links such as command uplink and telemetry downlink.

questions.stem: Why is thermal control needed for onboard electronics?
options: Electronic equipment has no lower temperature limit.
External heating is the only source of heat.
Components have acceptable operating-temperature ranges.
The same thermal design works at every operating condition.
questions.explanation: Thermal control helps keep equipment within its permitted temperature range despite changing inputs and internal heat.

questions.stem: What can a spacecraft deployment mechanism do?
options: Measure angular velocity
Unfold an antenna or solar array
Store electrical energy
Remove carbon dioxide from the cabin
questions.explanation: Deployment mechanisms move equipment from a launch configuration into its operational position.

questions.stem: How do a scientific payload and the spacecraft bus differ?
options: The payload performs mission-specific measurements; the bus provides supporting services.
The bus performs all mission measurements and the payload supplies only power.
The payload always provides the launch vehicle propulsion.
The bus can never communicate with the payload.
questions.explanation: The bus supplies shared functions such as power and communications while the payload carries out the mission purpose.

questions.stem: Which subsystem manages the cabin environment for a crew?
options: Attitude determination and control
Electrical power generation
Telemetry and command
Life support
questions.explanation: Crew life support manages needs such as breathable air and other cabin conditions.
